mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the prior quarter predicts a contractionary demand shock, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during episodes where both GDPC1 YoY < -2% and HOUST QoQ < -10%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5% for three consecutive months signals persistent labor market slack, which reduces corporate profit margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when UNRATE > 5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates a persistent contraction in manufacturing output, which depresses earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods of four consecutive months with INDPRO < -0.5% monthly change.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both CPIAUCSL (CPI) above 3% and FEDFUNDS above 4% for two consecutive months signals a dual shock of inflation and restrictive policy, which increases uncertainty and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3% AND FEDFUNDS > 4% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when both CPIAUCSL > 3% and FEDFUNDS > 4% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% combined with a monthly increase in retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% predicts a boost to consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% AND RSAFS monthly change > 1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during months where both PAYEMS and RSAFS show the specified increases.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) of more than 0.2 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which negatively impact corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE monthly change < -0.2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during three consecutive months of UNRATE monthly declines > 0.2pp.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation between monthly industrial production (INDPRO) growth and S&P 500 forward returns exists over the next 5 trading days, such that INDPRO monthly change > 0.3% predicts positive S&P 500 returns within the following week.
failure_condition: INDPRO monthly change > 0.3% fails to predict positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns with statistical significance (p > 0.10) in out-of-sample testing.
